assets.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: fine-pixel-art character study sheet, a preview for the creator to verify the SAME rabbit robot in three mechanical states.
Input images, all supplied by the creator and authorized for this rabbit only:
Image 1 = original pixel appearance reference: preserve its recognizable white face shape, large purple screen eyes, tiny triangular facial mark, black crown/hat silhouette, cyan-mint trim, and long floppy cyan mechanical rabbit ears. Ignore the cropped lettering, framing and backdrop.
Image 2 = rabbit anatomy and articulated landing-gear feet reference.
Image 3 = flight and hat-mounted propeller structure reference, including the colored small rabbit.
Image 4 = tail sphere opening and electrical discharge reference, plus rotor overview. Use its petal-opening ball ONLY as the tail; do not open the main body.
Primary request: Render this creator-owned character, Tian-shu Tia, faithfully as refined detailed PIXEL ART. Keep the reference's rabbit identity and characteristic face/panel pattern, not a newly redesigned generic orb drone.
Composition: a wide landscape sheet with THREE clearly separated equally sized views on one plain muted blue-gray background, no boxes and no lettering. All three are the exact same robot at the same body scale, complete within frame with generous margins.
Left: grounded, front three-quarter view; both long ears naturally droop; TWO small landing-gear legs extended with hinged foot pads as in Image 2; blades stowed; tail sphere closed and visible just behind the body.
Middle: flying, slight three-quarter view; feet retracted; thin blades extend radially from the outer rim of the hat/cap rotor. Central domed cap A remains seated on the head, at the SAME height as the grounded view. It can swivel independently but never spins together with the fast outer rotor B. Only outer rotor B and its extended blades rotate. No raised hat, no telescoping mast, no separate helicopter rotor above the hat. Tail closed, ears lowered.
Right: rear three-quarter view emphasizing the SMALL tail sphere connected to the back of the robot, with its shell petals opened and a small readable pale-cyan electric arc discharge; main body remains closed, feet extended for support, propeller stowed. Keep the face partly visible and keep the tail distinct from the feet.
Identity invariants: compact white-and-black spherical rabbit body, approximately 35 cm diameter as a working proportion; two elongated rounded-tip cyan-mint mechanical rabbit ears hinged on side joints, hanging downward rather than bird wings or fins. Purple eyes are cute and normally open; mechanical camera elements stay fully open and screen shapes convey expression. No humanoid torso, no hands, no furry animal anatomy, no extra limbs. Preserve reference details rather than inventing armor, antennas or ornaments.
Pixel finish: deliberate visible square pixel clusters and stepped edges, coherent limited color ramps, clean controlled light/shadow, enough resolution for ear hinges, face plates, foot pads and cap seams to remain readable. True pixel drawing language, not a smooth anime painting with a mosaic filter. Consistent pixel scale across all views.
Constraints: do not copy the source image layouts, screenshot borders, background text, labels or arrows. No humans, no extra characters, no floor scene, no weapons added beyond the specified tail discharge, no bottom thruster or fixed cylindrical dangling booster. No blur, 3D render, watermarks or text.
assets.review_status: superseded by targeted removal of unconfirmed rear sockets
visual_checks: Rabbit face, drooping ears, articulated feet, retractable rim blades and opened electrical tail are visible.
The three-view sheet is a draft, not a final website asset. Static views cannot prove rotor kinematics; text specification remains authoritative.
